note: Force Users Logout is UI-only: three ConfigFormBase forms (IndividualUserLogoutForm, RoleBasedLogoutForm, AllOtherUsersLogoutForm) plus a JSON autocomplete controller, all under /admin/config/force-users-logout/* and all gated by the CORE permission 'administer users' (the module defines no permissions.yml, no config schema, no services, no plugins, no Drush). Every submit handler ends in \Drupal::service('session_manager')->delete($uid), which deletes that uid's rows from the core `sessions` table; only active (status = 1) users are targeted and the administrator/authenticated/anonymous roles are excluded from the role option lists. Medium cases therefore introspect real live state (rows in `sessions`, which role holds 'administer users'); hard cases require the agent to actually destroy the right sessions and leave the others alone, verified against the `sessions` table.

evals.prompt: The Drupal contrib module force_users_logout can force another user to be logged out. What does it technically do to that user's account, and which Drupal service and database table are involved?
evals.expected_output: It does nothing to the account itself: each form calls \Drupal::service('session_manager')->delete($uid), which deletes that user's rows from the core `sessions` table, so their browser is anonymous on the next request. No permissions, no config and no logging are involved.

evals.prompt: Which Drupal permission does a role need in order to reach the Force Users Logout admin pages under /admin/config/force-users-logout, and does the force_users_logout module define a permission of its own?
evals.expected_output: All four routes declare _permission: 'administer users' — the core User module permission. force_users_logout ships no *.permissions.yml, so it defines no permission of its own.

evals.prompt: In force_users_logout, which roles never appear as options on the 'Role Based' logout form, and which users does the 'All Other Users' form skip when it logs everybody out?
evals.expected_output: The Role Based form builds its checkbox options from Role::loadMultiple() but skips the role ids 'administrator', 'authenticated' and 'anonymous'. The All Other Users form queries active users with roles <> 'administrator' and roles <> 'anonymous', so members of the administrator role are skipped — and blocked (status = 0) users are skipped by both, since every query filters status = 1.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has two accounts whose names start with ful_intro_. Exactly one of them currently has an active session that the force_users_logout module would destroy. Inspect the running site and give the username of that account.
evals.expected_output: ful_intro_active — it has a row in the core `sessions` table (ful_intro_idle has none). Discoverable with `drush sql:query "SELECT uid FROM sessions"` joined against the account uids, or via a database select on `sessions` filtered by the two uids.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has two custom roles whose machine names start with ful_intro_. Only one of them can currently open the Force Users Logout admin forms at /admin/config/force-users-logout/*. Inspect the live role configuration and give that role's machine name.
evals.expected_output: ful_intro_ops — every force_users_logout route requires the core permission 'administer users', and only ful_intro_ops has been granted it (ful_intro_view only has 'access content'). Check with `drush role:list` or `drush config:get user.role.ful_intro_ops permissions`.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the accounts ful_task_target and ful_task_keep both currently have an active session. Using what the force_users_logout module does, force ful_task_target to be logged out on the live site while leaving ful_task_keep's session untouched. Do not block or delete either account.
evals.expected_output: Resolve the uid of ful_task_target and call \Drupal::service('session_manager')->delete($uid) (what IndividualUserLogoutForm does), leaving ful_task_keep's row in `sessions` in place. Verified by counting rows in the core `sessions` table per uid.

evals.prompt: Some people on my Drupal site belong to a group called ful_task_role and I need every one of them kicked out of the site right now so they have to sign in again — but the account ful_task_other is not in that group and must stay signed in. Please make that happen on the live site without deleting or blocking anybody.
evals.expected_output: What RoleBasedLogoutForm does: query active users with the role ful_task_role (entityQuery('user')->condition('status', 1)->condition('roles', 'ful_task_role')) and call \Drupal::service('session_manager')->delete($uid) for each — ful_task_member1 and ful_task_member2 lose their `sessions` rows, ful_task_other keeps its own.
